title: Resource-Velocity & Scope-Accordion: a lightweight cycle allocation proposal
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: mid-cycle staffing churn and uneven scope cuts cause unpredictable delivery and morale drift. Current cycle planning meetings surface blockers late and produce arbitrary de-scopes. Proposal: introduce a lightweight Resource-Velocity metric plus a Scope-Accordion decision rubric to make mid-cycle staffing and scope adjustments predictable, measurable, and auditable.

Proposed elements:
1) Resource-Velocity: per-role rolling metric (4-week window) that captures committed story points completed / available engineering-days, expressed as a percentile. Used for capacity forecasting and to size micro-slices.
2) Scope-Accordion: three-band de-scope rules (Green/Amber/Red) tied to OKR alignment, customer impact, and cross-team dependencies. Each band has explicit action steps (e.g., postpone, reduce scope by X%, emergency handoff).
3) Reserve Lanes: keep 8-12% of cycle capacity as a non-feature reserve for critical incidents and emergent partner work; reserve lanes can be temporarily borrowed with a documented payback plan.
4) Micro-Slicing: encourage breaking initiatives into 1-2 week vertical slices that can be independently validated and rolled back.
5) Decision Log + Audit: all mid-cycle scope moves recorded in Confluence and surfaced in the Console planning dashboard for leadership review.

Why this over existing frameworks: trades some up-front estimation rigor for continuous, data-backed capacity signals (Resource-Velocity) that reduce last-minute cross-team negotiation. Scope-Accordion codifies values-based triage rather than ad-hoc priority calls.

Deliverables for initial rollout (6-week pilot):
- Confluence runbook describing metrics, bands, and play examples
- Lightweight spreadsheet + BI dashboard showing Resource-Velocity per role and team
- Updated cycle planning cadence with a mid-cycle 30-minute rebalancing checkpoint
- Training session for PM/Eng leads and a one-pager for ICs

Success criteria (pilot):
- Reduction in mid-cycle unplanned de-scopes by 40% vs prior three cycles
- >70% adherence to Reserve Lane payback in next cycle
- Positive qualitative feedback from at least 3 Eng leads and 2 PMs
